’Opakapaka projections: MVN vs MCMC uncertainty

Overview

This vignette carries the ’opakapaka (Pristipomoides filamentosus) case study forward from estimation into projection. It reuses the opal with length compositions model (obj_lf) developed in vignette("opakapaka") — the assessment that fits both CPUE indices and length compositions and estimates selectivity — and projects the stock forward under a constant-catch scenario, propagating parameter uncertainty two ways:

  1. MVN simulation — multivariate-normal draws from the Hessian-derived variance-covariance matrix at the MLE; no MCMC required.
  2. MCMC posteriors — draws from the joint posterior obtained via SparseNUTS (code shown; a cached fit is loaded by default).

The historical spawning-biomass uncertainty is shown with the delta method (sdreport) for the MVN case and with posterior trajectory quantiles for the MCMC case. Both are bridged continuously into the projection period so the terminal-state uncertainty and the future process uncertainty are visible on a single axis. The Stock Synthesis 3 operating-model (OM) and estimation-model (EM) spawning-biomass trajectories are overlaid over the historical period for reference.

See vignette("opakapaka") for the full model configuration, biological inputs, and cross-platform benchmarking; only the elements needed to build obj_lf are reproduced here.

Setup 

library(opal)
library(RTMB)
library(SparseNUTS)
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)

theme_set(theme_bw())

# The MCMC fit is pre-computed and loaded from the package (see the
# `mcmc-sampling` chunk, which is disabled); n_chains_mcmc must match the
# number of chains used to produce the cached fit.
n_chains_mcmc <- 8L

Data, parameters, and map

The data preparation, parameter list, priors, and parameter map are identical to the opal with LF model in vignette("opakapaka"). They are reproduced compactly below.

data(opaka_data)
data <- opaka_data
if (is.null(data$n_index)) data$n_index <- 2L
data$priors  <- NULL

# Anchor the growth curve at biological age 0 (SS3 indexes ages 0-43)
data$A1      <- 0
data$A2      <- data$A1 + (data$n_age - 1)
data$min_age <- 0
ages <- data$age_a <- seq(data$min_age, by = 1, length.out = data$n_age)
data$sex_ratio <- rep(1, data$n_age)

# Length composition data (Comm = fleet 1, ResFish = fleet 3)
data(opaka_lf)
lf_wide <- opaka_lf %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(fishery, year, month, ts),
                     names_from = bin, values_from = value, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(fishery, ts)
data <- prep_lf_data(data, lf_wide,
                     lf_keep_fisheries = c(1, 3),
                     lf_var_adjust     = 1 / rep(1, data$n_fishery),
                     lf_addtocomp      = 1e-10)

# Calendar years for the modelled period (1949-2023)
calendar_years <- (1949 - 1) + data$years

# SS3-style recruitment bias-adjustment ramps
init_cohort_years <- 1949 - (data$age_a - 1)
data$init_bias_adj_a <- get_bias_adj_vector(
  years = init_cohort_years, do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,
  bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43), max_bias_adj = 0.869)
data$bias_adj_y <- get_bias_adj_vector(
  years = calendar_years, do_rec_bias_ramp = 1,
  bias_years = c(1931, 1974, 2021.88, 2022.43), max_bias_adj = 0.869)
data(opaka_parameters)

# Route the 1949 deviate to the age-0 cohort; shift 1950-2023 into rdev_y and
# append a terminal 0 (see the opakapaka vignette for the full rationale).
init_rdev_a <- rev(c(0.0206807,0.00321579,0.00372620,0.0043174,0.00500263,
  0.00579674,0.00671727,0.00778422,0.00902081,0.0104539,0.0121143,0.0140375,
  0.0162641,0.0188404,0.0218182,0.0252561,0.0292182,0.0337726,0.0389898,
  0.0449362,0.0516662,0.0592049,0.0675236,0.0764992,0.0858443,0.0950047,
  0.102706,0.107687,0.107712,0.0998349,0.0808137,0.0482339,0.00234443,
  -0.0517563,-0.102395,-0.131458,-0.121101,-0.0714826,-0.00742166,-0.0109308,
  -0.0385029,0.0366483,0.0165105,-0.166906))
init_rdev_a[1]   <- opaka_parameters$rdev_y[1]
rdev_y_shifted   <- c(opaka_parameters$rdev_y[2:length(opaka_parameters$rdev_y)], 0.0)

parameters <- list(
  log_B0         = 9,
  log_h          = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_h),
  log_sigma_r    = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_sigma_r),
  log_cpue_q     = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_q),
  log_cpue_tau   = rep(log(0.1), data$n_index),
  log_cpue_omega = as.numeric(rep(opaka_parameters$log_cpue_omega, data$n_index)),
  log_lf_tau     = as.numeric(log(rep(0.1, data$n_fishery))),
  log_L1         = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L1),
  log_L2         = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_L2),
  log_k          = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_k),
  log_CV1        = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV1),
  log_CV2        = as.numeric(opaka_parameters$log_CV2),
  par_sel        = as.matrix(opaka_parameters$par_sel),
  log_init_F_f   = c(log(0.0119122), rep(log(1e-8), data$n_fishery - 1)),
  rdev_y         = rdev_y_shifted,
  init_rdev_a    = init_rdev_a
)
parameters$par_sel <- convert_ss3_selex_to_rtmb(parameters$par_sel,
                                                data$sel_type_f, data$len_mid)

data$priors <- get_priors(parameters = parameters, data = data)

The parameter map frees B0B_0, the two CPUE catchabilities, all recruitment and initial-age deviations, and the two Comm logistic + three ResFish double-normal selectivity parameters. Steepness, σR\sigma_R, growth, and the non-commercial selectivity are fixed at SS3 values.

map_sel <- matrix(NA, nrow(parameters$par_sel), ncol(parameters$par_sel))
map_sel[1, 1:2]        <- c(1, 2)   # Comm logistic
map_sel[3, c(1, 4, 6)] <- c(3, 4, 5) # ResFish double-normal
map_sel <- as.vector(map_sel)

map <- list(
  log_h          = factor(NA),
  log_sigma_r    = factor(NA),
  log_cpue_tau   = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),
  log_cpue_omega = factor(rep(NA, data$n_index)),
  log_lf_tau     = factor(rep(NA, length(parameters$log_lf_tau))),
  log_L1  = factor(NA), log_L2 = factor(NA), log_k = factor(NA),
  log_CV1 = factor(NA), log_CV2 = factor(NA),
  par_sel      = factor(map_sel),
  log_init_F_f = rep(factor(NA), data$n_fishery),
  init_rdev_a  = as.factor(seq_len(data$n_age)),
  rdev_y       = as.factor(seq_len(length(parameters$rdev_y)))
)

Build and optimise 

data$lf_switch <- 1L   # multinomial length-composition likelihood

obj_lf <- MakeADFun(func = cmb(opal_model, data), parameters = parameters,
                    map = map)

Lwr <- rep(-Inf, length(obj_lf$par)); Upr <- rep(Inf, length(obj_lf$par))
Lwr[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(1)
Upr[grep("log_B0",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(exp(22))
Lwr[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(0.001)
Upr[grep("log_cpue_q",  names(obj_lf$par))] <- log(10)
Lwr[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5
Upr[grep("rdev_y",      names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5
Lwr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <- -5
Upr[grep("init_rdev_a", names(obj_lf$par))] <-  5
Lwr[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <- -7
Upr[grep("par_sel",     names(obj_lf$par))] <-  7

control <- list(eval.max = 10000, iter.max = 10000)
opt <- nlminb(obj_lf$par, obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,
              control = control)
opt <- nlminb(opt$par,    obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,
              control = control)
opt <- nlminb(opt$par,    obj_lf$fn, obj_lf$gr, lower = Lwr, upper = Upr,
              control = control)

cat("Convergence:", opt$convergence, "\n")
cat("Max gradient:", max(abs(obj_lf$gr())), "\n")
cat("NLL:", opt$objective, "\n")

Historical uncertainty (delta method)

ADREPORT(spawning_biomass_y) is registered inside do_dynamics(), so sdreport() propagates Hessian uncertainty through the full historical spawning-biomass trajectory via automatic differentiation. These delta-method standard errors are used later for the MVN historical ribbon.

sdr       <- RTMB::sdreport(obj_lf)
sdr_sum   <- summary(sdr, "report")
sbio_rows <- which(rownames(sdr_sum) == "spawning_biomass_y")
sbio_mle_sd <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Estimate"]
sbio_se_sd  <- sdr_sum[sbio_rows, "Std. Error"]

# Scalar parameter SEs from the inverse Hessian (for reference)
H_lf   <- obj_lf$he(); Sigma <- solve(H_lf); SE_vec <- sqrt(diag(Sigma))
mu_vec <- obj_lf$env$last.par.best

The MLE B0B_0 and the estimated terminal spawning biomass:

B0_est   <- obj_lf$report()$B0
term_idx <- data$n_year + 1
cat("B0 (MLE):", round(B0_est), "mt\n")
cat("Terminal SB:", round(sbio_mle_sd[term_idx]),
    "+/-", round(sbio_se_sd[term_idx]), "mt (delta-method SE)\n")
cat("Terminal depletion SB/B0:", round(sbio_mle_sd[term_idx] / B0_est, 3), "\n")

Forward projections

Common setup

The projection holds catch constant at the terminal year’s level across a 10-year horizon. Projected recruitment deviates are simulated from an ARIMA model fitted to the estimated rdev_y series; projected selectivity replicates the mean selectivity over the last ten estimated years.

# Fields required by the projection helpers
data$first_yr         <- 1949L
data$last_yr          <- 2023L
data$removal_switch_f <- rep(0L, data$n_fishery)

n_proj <- 10    # projection years
n_iter <- 200   # uncertainty iterations

# Projected recruitment deviates (ARIMA on the fitted MLE series)
rdev_proj <- project_rec_devs(
  data = data, obj = obj_lf, first_yr = data$first_yr,
  n_proj = n_proj, n_iter = n_iter)

# Projected selectivity (mean of the last 10 estimated years, per iteration)
sel_proj <- project_selectivity(
  data = data, obj = obj_lf, first_yr = data$last_yr - 9,
  n_proj = n_proj, n_iter = n_iter)

# Constant-catch scenario: hold catch at the last observed year's level
catch_ysf_proj <- array(0, dim = c(n_proj, data$n_season, data$n_fishery))
for (y in seq_len(n_proj)) {
  catch_ysf_proj[y, , ] <- data$catch_obs_ysf[data$n_year, , ]
}

Approach 1: MVN simulation

With mcmc = NULL, project_dynamics() draws parameter sets from a multivariate-normal centred on the MLE, using the inverse Hessian as the covariance. Positive parameters already on the log scale (log_B0, log_cpue_q) are drawn in log-space; the recruitment and initial-age deviations (rdev_y, init_rdev_a) and the selectivity working-scale parameters (par_sel) are drawn on their natural unbounded scale. To avoid a Jensen’s-inequality inflation of mean biomass, each deviation is set to its conditional expectation given the drawn scalar parameters, which preserves the negative B0↔B_0 \leftrightarrow deviation correlation and aligns the bridge point with the delta-method historical ribbon.

proj_mvn <- project_dynamics(
  data      = data,
  object    = obj_lf,
  mcmc      = NULL,             # triggers the MVN path
  n_proj    = n_proj,
  n_iter    = n_iter,
  rdev_y    = rdev_proj$rdev_y,
  sel_fya   = sel_proj,
  catch_ysf = catch_ysf_proj
)

Approach 2: MCMC posteriors

A No-U-Turn sampler chain is run via SparseNUTS with a dense mass matrix. The opal_globals() call exports the model-agnostic helper functions needed for likelihood evaluation inside the MCMC workers. Because both CPUE indices and the length compositions inform the fit, the B0B_0/qq scale is well identified and no additional priors are needed beyond those already in the model.

n_chains_mcmc <- 8
mcmc_fit <- SparseNUTS::sample_snuts(
  obj         = obj_lf,
  globals     = opal_globals(),
  num_samples = 750,
  num_warmup  = 1500,
  chains      = n_chains_mcmc,
  cores       = min(n_chains_mcmc, parallel::detectCores()),
  metric      = "dense",
  seed        = 42,
  # A high adapt_delta and deeper trees are needed for this posterior: with the
  # default settings the survey length-composition geometry produces divergences
  # and elevated Rhat.
  control     = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 12)
)
saveRDS(mcmc_fit, "inst/extdata/opaka_mcmc_fit.rds")
mcmc_fit <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "opaka_mcmc_fit.rds", package = "opal"))

For the MCMC path, projected recruitment deviates are generated by fitting an ARIMA model to each posterior draw’s own historical rdev_y series, so the projected recruitment pattern stays consistent with the historical pattern for that draw.

rdev_proj_mcmc <- project_rec_devs(
  data = data, obj = obj_lf, mcmc = mcmc_fit,
  first_yr = data$first_yr, n_proj = n_proj, n_iter = n_iter)
proj_mcmc <- project_dynamics(
  data        = data,
  object      = obj_lf,
  mcmc        = mcmc_fit,       # triggers the MCMC path
  n_proj      = n_proj,
  n_iter      = n_iter,
  rdev_y      = rdev_proj_mcmc$rdev_y,
  sel_fya     = sel_proj,
  catch_ysf   = catch_ysf_proj,
  return_hist = TRUE            # collect historical SB per posterior draw
)

MCMC diagnostics

Split-chain R̂\hat{R} and effective sample sizes for the scalar parameters and a spread of recruitment deviates confirm convergence before the projection envelopes are compared.

post_samples <- SparseNUTS::extract_samples(mcmc_fit)
n_post_total <- nrow(post_samples)
n_per_chain  <- n_post_total / n_chains_mcmc
chain_id     <- rep(seq_len(n_chains_mcmc), each = n_per_chain)
iter_id      <- rep(seq_len(n_per_chain),   times = n_chains_mcmc)

rdev_idx_all  <- grep("rdev_y", colnames(post_samples))
rdev_idx_show <- rdev_idx_all[round(seq(1, length(rdev_idx_all), length.out = 4))]
diag_cols     <- c("log_B0", "log_cpue_q[1]", "log_cpue_q[2]",
                   colnames(post_samples)[rdev_idx_show])

draws_df <- as.data.frame(post_samples[, diag_cols, drop = FALSE])
draws_df[[".chain"]]     <- chain_id
draws_df[[".iteration"]] <- iter_id
draws_obj <- posterior::as_draws_df(draws_df)
diag_tbl  <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  draws_obj,
  posterior::default_summary_measures(),
  posterior::default_convergence_measures())
diag_tbl$mle <- mu_vec[match(diag_tbl$variable, names(mu_vec))]

knitr::kable(
  diag_tbl[, c("variable", "mle", "mean", "sd", "q5", "q95",
               "ess_bulk", "ess_tail", "rhat")],
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0("MCMC diagnostics for key parameters (split-chain Rhat and ",
                   "ESS). ESS < 100 or Rhat > 1.01 indicate poor convergence."))

SparseNUTS::check_snuts_diagnostics(mcmc_fit)
trace_df <- data.frame(
  iter  = iter_id, chain = factor(chain_id),
  log_B0        = post_samples[, "log_B0"],
  `log_cpue_q1` = post_samples[, "log_cpue_q[1]"],
  `log_cpue_q2` = post_samples[, "log_cpue_q[2]"],
  check.names = FALSE) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(iter, chain), names_to = "param", values_to = "value")

mle_ref <- data.frame(
  param = c("log_B0", "log_cpue_q1", "log_cpue_q2"),
  mle   = c(mu_vec["log_B0"], mu_vec[names(mu_vec) == "log_cpue_q"]))

ggplot(trace_df, aes(iter, value, colour = chain)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(data = mle_ref, aes(yintercept = mle),
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ param, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Post-warmup iteration", y = "Value", colour = "Chain")

Comparison: MVN vs MCMC uncertainty

Projected spawning biomass is extracted from each iteration and summarised as quantile envelopes. number_ysa[1, , ] is the terminal historical state (proj_year = 0), so it bridges continuously to the historical trajectory.

spa <- obj_lf$report()$spawning_potential_a

sbio_df <- function(proj_list, label) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(proj_list), function(i) {
    dyn <- proj_list[[i]]
    sb  <- sapply(1:(n_proj + 1), function(y) sum(dyn$number_ysa[y, 1, ] * spa))
    data.frame(iter = i, proj_year = 0:n_proj, sbio = sb, method = label)
  }))
}

df_mvn  <- sbio_df(proj_mvn,      "MVN")
df_mcmc <- sbio_df(proj_mcmc$dyn, "MCMC")
df_all  <- rbind(df_mvn, df_mcmc)
# Map model timesteps to calendar years: historical t = 1..(n_year+1) -> 1948+t
# (t = n_year+1 is the terminal state = 2024); projection proj_year p -> 2024+p
n_hist_show <- 60L
hist_idx    <- (term_idx - n_hist_show + 1):term_idx
hist_years  <- 1948L + hist_idx

# MVN historical ribbon: delta-method Gaussian CI (no Jensen bias)
df_hist_mvn <- data.frame(
  year = hist_years,
  med  = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx],
  lo50 = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx] - qnorm(0.75) * sbio_se_sd[hist_idx],
  hi50 = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx] + qnorm(0.75) * sbio_se_sd[hist_idx],
  lo90 = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx] - qnorm(0.95) * sbio_se_sd[hist_idx],
  hi90 = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx] + qnorm(0.95) * sbio_se_sd[hist_idx],
  method = "MVN")

# MCMC historical ribbon: posterior trajectory quantiles
hist_ribbon <- function(hist_sbio, label, idx, years) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(idx), function(k) {
    v <- hist_sbio[, idx[k]]
    data.frame(year = years[k],
               med  = median(v, na.rm = TRUE),
               lo50 = quantile(v, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
               hi50 = quantile(v, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
               lo90 = quantile(v, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
               hi90 = quantile(v, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
               method = label)
  }))
}
df_hist_mcmc   <- hist_ribbon(proj_mcmc$hist_sbio, "MCMC", hist_idx, hist_years)
df_hist_ribbon <- rbind(df_hist_mvn, df_hist_mcmc)

# Projection quantile ribbons (proj_year = 0 -> 2024 bridge point)
df_ribbon <- df_all |>
  filter(!is.na(sbio)) |>
  group_by(method, proj_year) |>
  summarise(med  = median(sbio, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo50 = quantile(sbio, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi50 = quantile(sbio, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo90 = quantile(sbio, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi90 = quantile(sbio, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(!is.na(med)) |>
  mutate(year = 2024L + proj_year)

# MLE historical line + SS3 references
hist_mle_df <- data.frame(year = hist_years, sbio = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx])
data(opaka_truth)
ss3_om <- subset(opaka_truth$om$sprseries, Yr %in% hist_years)
ss3_em <- subset(opaka_truth$em$sprseries, Yr %in% hist_years)
pal <- c(MVN = "steelblue", MCMC = "darkorange")

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_hist_ribbon,
              aes(year, ymin = lo90, ymax = hi90, fill = method), alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_hist_ribbon,
              aes(year, ymin = lo50, ymax = hi50, fill = method), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = subset(df_hist_ribbon, method == "MCMC"),
            aes(year, med, colour = method), linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_line(data = hist_mle_df, aes(year, sbio), colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(data = ss3_om, aes(Yr, SSB), colour = "black",
            linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = ss3_em, aes(Yr, SSB), colour = "red", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2024, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_ribbon,
              aes(year, ymin = lo90, ymax = hi90, fill = method), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_ribbon,
              aes(year, ymin = lo50, ymax = hi50, fill = method), alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_line(data = df_ribbon, aes(year, med, colour = method), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Spawning biomass (mt)", colour = "Method", fill = "Method")
B0_mcmc      <- exp(post_samples[, "log_B0"])
B0_mcmc_iter <- B0_mcmc[seq_len(n_iter)]

# Historical depletion
df_hist_mvn_dep <- df_hist_mvn |>
  mutate(across(c(med, lo50, hi50, lo90, hi90), ~ . / B0_est))
hist_sbio_dep    <- sweep(proj_mcmc$hist_sbio, 1, B0_mcmc_iter, "/")
df_hist_mcmc_dep <- hist_ribbon(hist_sbio_dep, "MCMC", hist_idx, hist_years)
df_hist_ribbon_dep <- rbind(df_hist_mvn_dep, df_hist_mcmc_dep)

# Projection depletion
df_ribbon_mvn_dep <- df_ribbon |>
  filter(method == "MVN") |>
  mutate(across(c(med, lo50, hi50, lo90, hi90), ~ . / B0_est))
df_ribbon_mcmc_dep <- df_mcmc |>
  mutate(sbio = sbio / B0_mcmc[iter]) |>
  filter(!is.na(sbio)) |>
  group_by(method, proj_year) |>
  summarise(med  = median(sbio, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo50 = quantile(sbio, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi50 = quantile(sbio, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
            lo90 = quantile(sbio, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
            hi90 = quantile(sbio, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(!is.na(med)) |>
  mutate(year = 2024L + proj_year)
df_ribbon_dep <- rbind(df_ribbon_mvn_dep, df_ribbon_mcmc_dep)

hist_mle_dep <- data.frame(year = hist_years, dep = sbio_mle_sd[hist_idx] / B0_est)

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_hist_ribbon_dep,
              aes(year, ymin = lo90, ymax = hi90, fill = method), alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_hist_ribbon_dep,
              aes(year, ymin = lo50, ymax = hi50, fill = method), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = subset(df_hist_ribbon_dep, method == "MCMC"),
            aes(year, med, colour = method), linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_line(data = hist_mle_dep, aes(year, dep), colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2024, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_ribbon_dep,
              aes(year, ymin = lo90, ymax = hi90, fill = method), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_ribbon(data = df_ribbon_dep,
              aes(year, ymin = lo50, ymax = hi50, fill = method), alpha = 0.30) +
  geom_line(data = df_ribbon_dep, aes(year, med, colour = method), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.2, linetype = "dotted", colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = expression("Relative depletion (SB / B"[0]*")"),
       colour = "Method", fill = "Method")

Reading the bridge point. In the MVN case the scalar parameters are drawn from the Hessian and each deviation is pinned to its conditional expectation, so the proj_year = 0 ribbon coincides with the delta-method (sdreport) historical ribbon. In the MCMC case each draw carries its own full history, so the bridge-point spread reflects the actual posterior uncertainty in the current biomass state. Because ‘opakapaka is long-lived and matures slowly, the existing adult stock declines nearly deterministically under constant catch, and the two methods’ projection envelopes widen only gradually as future recruitment and selectivity uncertainty accumulate.

df_all |>
  filter(proj_year == n_proj, !is.na(sbio)) |>
  group_by(method) |>
  summarise(mean   = mean(sbio),
            sd     = sd(sbio),
            p05    = quantile(sbio, 0.05),
            median = median(sbio),
            p95    = quantile(sbio, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
    caption = paste0("Projected spawning biomass (mt) at year ", 2024 + n_proj,
                     " under constant catch, by uncertainty method."))
